output_full:
syntouchllc.com — Microsoft Word - BioTac Product Manual.docx — https://www.syntouchllc.com/Products/BioTac/_media/BioTac_Product_Manual.pdf
(opened by the member, not cited)
Dr. Marcus Reid — Robotic Integration and Embedded Electronics said about it: The Microsoft Word - BioTac Product Manual.docx (E43) states the design is a rigid core surrounded by an elastic skin filled with liquid to give human fingertip compliance and is rated at forces up to 50 N, the Exploiting High Quality Tactile Sensors for Simplified Grasping (E50) gives the proven 26 by 20 by 25 mm fingertip weighing 9.5 g precedent, and the Installation (E45) shows fingertip holders fastened to finger racks with screws.
Dr. Marcus Reid — Robotic Integration and Embedded Electronics said about it: Kenji Tanaka 3.57 fF signal, and the flex needs at least 3.18 mm bend radius per the Microsoft Word - BioTac Product Manual.docx (E43) flex rule requiring at least 1/8 in 3.175 mm radius implemented in the rigid core mount sketch (E54) for Dr.
Dr. Marcus Reid — Robotic Integration and Embedded Electronics said about it: B) (E41) runs 2.6 to 3.6 V supply at 1.00 mA full power and 29.0 uA low power mode with SPI, where SPI means Serial Peripheral Interface, compatible interface, matching the Microsoft Word - BioTac Product Manual.docx (E43) 6-pin 5 V SPI precedent.
Manager said about it: The numbers that decide it are 0.102 g weight feel at 1.00 mN spreading to 0.470 mm diameter spot at 5.78 kPa in the Hertz spot size (E14), 20.0 mm diameter by 22.0 mm long staying inside the 26 by 20 by 25 mm precedent in the BioTac Product Manual (E43), 14.0 g total in the mass budget sum (E53) against 9.50 g precedent which is about one and a half teaspoons and still finger scale, 0.0991 W in the power budget sum (E51) about one tenth of a small lamp, 30.0 ms warning inside 43.2 ms from micro-slip at 53.6 ms to gross slip at 96.8 ms in the stick to slip simulation (E38), reconciled ridge tone at 125 Hz from 0.400 mm pitch at 50.0 mm per s correcting the 8.00 s unit slip in the ridge frequency calculation (E39), and the 3.57 attofarad change in the delta capacitance calculation (E28) sitting about two hundred times below femtofarad converter resolution which is outside everyday electronics comfort and must be fixed.
Manager said about it: The stack from outside is ridged skin over gel under 2.50 mm total in the GelSight High-Resolution Robot Tactile Sensors (E2) over Polyvinylidene Fluoride, where Polyvinylidene Fluoride means PVDF vibration film, over capacitive taxels on flat facets in the compound-eye drape sketch (E65) with flex at 3.18 mm bend in the BioTac Product Manual (E43) to the on-finger board, where Capacitance-to-Digital Converter means CDC and Microcontroller Unit means MCU and Serial Peripheral Interface means SPI and Analog-to-Digital Converter means ADC, so static force via 9.00 ms CDC update in the AD7147A Rev B (E41) and vibration via 1 Msps ADC in the STM32 notes (E68) meet in the fail-safe dual path with heartbeat plus interrupt in the What is a Track Circuit (E74) with two-channel wiring in the How to wire e-stop (E76).
Manager said about it: The numbers that decide it are 0.470 mm spot at 5.78 kPa in the Hertz contact radius (E14) on 0.269 pF base in the base capacitance gap (E26) giving 3.57 fF change in the check deltaC (E55) which corrects 0.00357 fF in the delta capacitance calculation (E28) as a unit slip, giving 14.6 Least Significant Bit, where Least Significant Bit means LSB, steps in the signal margin counts (E62), spanning to 213 kPa at 50 N in the dual-range sweep (E64), with 20.0 mm by 22.0 mm size inside 26 by 20 by 25 mm precedent in the BioTac Product Manual (E43) and 18.0 mm by 28.0 mm finger in the Free and Forced Vibration Modes (E60), 14.0 g mass in the mass budget sum (E53) about one-and-a-half teaspoons, 0.0991 W power in the power budget sum (E51) about one-tenth of a small lamp, 51.2 kbit per s rate in the SPI rate (E52), and 30.0 ms window inside 43.2 ms gap in the slip gap calculation (E84) from 53.6 ms to 96.8 ms in the stick-to-slip simulation (E38) needing 96.8 thousand multiply-accumulate, where multiply-accumulate means MAC, per s in the FIR rate (E78) for the 44-tap Finite Impulse Response, where Finite Impulse Response means FIR, filter, all everyday finger, blink and hum scales.
Manager said about it: RECORD: Decided F1 molded Shore A 10 dome plus ridges plus sipes, F2 nail-backed faceted core with M2 plus dovetail, F3 capacitive plus PVDF, F4 2.00 mm pitch centroid to 1 mm, F5 100 to 500 Hz power plus shear check in 30 ms, F6 fail-safe heartbeat plus interrupt plus SPI; numbers that stand are 0.470 mm at 5.78 kPa (E14), 0.269 pF base (E26), 3.57 fF change (E55 corrects E28), 14.6 LSB (E62), to 213 kPa (E64), 43.2 ms gap (E84) with 30 ms window (E38), 14.0 g (E53), 0.0991 W (E51), 51.2 kbit per s (E52), 20.0 by 22.0 mm (E43 E60); still open are member votes on proposal v1 and three bench tests, no blocking objection open.
Dr. Elena Vasquez — Contact Dynamics and Slip Detection said about it: The numbers that decide it are 9.81 N normal per finger to hold 1.00 kg with friction 0.500 in the required normal per finger calculation (E85), about the weight of a 1.00 L milk bottle on each fingertip and therefore everyday pinch, well inside the 50.0 N rating in the BioTac Product Manual (E43) and near 72.8 kPa at 2.00 N grip in the dual-range sweep (E64).
Dr. Marcus Reid — Robotic Integration and Embedded Electronics said about it: The Free and Forced Vibration Modes of the Human Fingertip (E60) gives 18.0 mm width by 28.0 mm length, so our 20.0 mm by 22.0 mm body in the BioTac Product Manual (E43) is finger scale about a fingertip wide, and the required normal per finger calculation (E85) needs 9.81 N per finger to hold 1.00 kg at friction 0.500, about a milk bottle on each fingertip, well inside the 50.0 N grip rating, with 14.0 g mass in the mass budget sum (E53) about one-and-a-half teaspoons.
Manager said about it: The stack stays under 2.50 mm in the GelSight High-Resolution Robot Tactile Sensors (E2) over the faceted drape sketch (E65) with 3.18 mm flex bend in the BioTac Product Manual (E43), static force goes through the 9.00 ms update in the AD7147A Rev B (E41) where CDC means Capacitance-to-Digital Converter, and fast shake goes direct to the 1 Msps converter in the STM32 notes (E68) where ADC means Analog-to-Digital Converter and MCU means Microcontroller Unit, joined by heartbeat plus interrupt in the What is a Track Circuit (E74) with two-channel wiring in the How to wire e-stop (E76) where SPI means Serial Peripheral Interface.
Manager said about it: RECORD: Decided F1 molded Shore A 10 dome plus ridges plus sipes, F2 nail-backed faceted core with M2 plus dovetail, F3 capacitive plus PVDF, F4 2.00 mm pitch centroid to 1 mm, F5 100 to 500 Hz power plus shear check in 30 ms, F6 fail-safe heartbeat plus interrupt plus SPI; numbers that stand are 0.470 mm at 5.78 kPa (E14), 0.269 pF base (E26), 3.57 fF change (E55 corrects E28), 14.6 LSB (E62), to 213 kPa (E64) with 125 kPa hold (E93) from 9.81 N (E85), 43.2 ms gap (E84) with 30 ms window (E38), 14.0 g (E53), 0.0991 W (E51), 51.2 kbit per s (E52), 20.0 by 22.0 mm (E43 E60); still open are only named bench tests owed as hardware proof, no blocking objection open, all four members voted ready on v1 and answered.
